title: Etale multisections avoid nodes on a regular nodal trait family
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:W\to S$ be flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with nodal geometric curve fibres and smooth generic fibre. Assume that $W$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $B\to S$ be finite etale [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism], allowing $B=\varnothing$. Every $S$-morphism $b:B\to W$ factors through the relative smooth locus of $f$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. In particular, every section $S\to W$ lies in that locus. Here nodal geometric curve fibres means reduced geometric fibres of pure dimension one whose nonsmooth closed points over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ have completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-pure-dimension, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]; the fibres may be disconnected.

source.place: Agent consequence of Tag 0CDD (lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal), nonzero-parameter case, and Tag 0CDC (example-blowup), regularity of xy=pi^n; extracted valuation argument from expanded common-model step 8. proof.text: Let $W^{\mathrm{sm}}$ be the union of the open neighbourhoods on which $f$ is smooth. Thus a point belongs to this open precisely when $f$ is smooth there. By [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion], every point over the generic point of $S$ belongs to it: $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and the generic fibre is smooth. It suffices to rule out a point $\beta\in B$ above the closed point of $S$ for which $w=b(\beta)$ is nonsmooth. Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$. Apply [lem-sfb-trait-nodal-etale-dvr-model] at $w$. All its geometric-fibre hypotheses are those of the item, and the generic fibre is smooth. Obtain an etale local extension of DVRs $R\to R'$, with the image of $\pi$ still a uniformizer, a point $u\in U$ over $w$, and etale maps $p:U\to W$ and $q:U\to M_n=\operatorname{Spec}R'[x,y]/(xy-\pi^n)$ over $S$, with $n\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 0CDD, lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal; smooth-generic refinement in Tag 0CDE, lemma-blowup-at-worst-nodal, first proof paragraph; morphisms.tex Tag 01V9

proof.text: The point $q(u)$ is the origin $o=(\pi,x,y)$. Indeed it lies in the special fibre, since $u$ maps to $w$. By [lem-sfb-binomial-geometric-fibres], the special fibre of $M_n/R'$ is smooth off its crossing. Since $M_n/R'$ is flat and finitely presented by [lem-sfb-dvr-binomial-local-geometry], [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion] makes $M_n\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$ smooth at any other special-fibre point. The etale map $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to S$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres], so [lem-trf-smooth-composition] makes $M_n\to S$ smooth near such a point. If $q(u)\ne o$, the pointwise assertion of [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness], applied first to $q$ and then to $p$, would make $f$ smooth at $w$, a contradiction.

source.place: Tag 0CDC, example-blowup, local models; morphisms.tex Tags 01V9 and 01VA; descent.tex Tag 036U

proof.text: Regularity of $W$ implies that $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ is regular. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-stalk-invariants] to $p$ to deduce regularity of $\mathcal O_{U,u}$, then to $q$ to deduce regularity of $\mathcal O_{M_n,o}$. The final assertion of [lem-sfb-dvr-binomial-local-geometry] says that this local ring is regular exactly for $n=1$. Hence the chart equation is $xy=\pi$, with $x$ and $y$ vanishing at $q(u)=o$.

source.place: Tag 0CDC, example-blowup, regularity at the origin; more-algebra.tex Tag 0AH0, lemma-regular-etale-extension

proof.text: Form $T=B\times_WU$. The two points $\beta$ and $u$ have common image $w$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points], the points of $T$ over both are in bijection with $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(\beta)\otimes_{\kappa(w)}\kappa(u))$; this tensor product of two nonzero vector spaces over the field $\kappa(w)$ is a nonzero ring, so it has a prime ideal, giving a point $t\in T$ above both. The projection $T\to B$ is etale by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. Since $B\to S$ is etale, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] makes $T\to S$ etale. The point $t$ lies above the closed point of $S$. Apply [lem-sbc-etale-trait-stalk] to this very morphism and point. It gives the actual ring $D=\mathcal O_{T,t}$, a domain DVR, and its canonical injective structural map $\delta:R\to D$, with $\mathfrak m_D=(\delta(\pi))$.

source.place: Tag 0AP2, lemma-Dedekind-etale-extension, scheme-stalk version; morphisms.tex Tags 02GO and 02GN; schemes.tex Tag 01JT, lemma-points-fibre-product

proof.text: Pull back the functions $x,y$ from $M_1$ along $T\to U\to M_1$ and then to $D$. Call their images $a,c$. Because $t$ maps to $u$ and then to $o$, both $a,c$ lie in $\mathfrak m_D$. Compatibility over $S$ gives $ac=\delta(\pi)$. Put $\varpi=\delta(\pi)$. The equality $\mathfrak m_D=(\varpi)$ gives $a=\varpi a_1$ and $c=\varpi c_1$ for some $a_1,c_1\in D$. Thus $\varpi=\varpi^2a_1c_1$. The element $\varpi$ is nonzero by injectivity of $\delta$ and nonzeroness of a DVR uniformizer. Cancellation in the domain $D$ gives $1=\varpi a_1c_1\in\mathfrak m_D$, contradicting that a maximal ideal is proper. This is the elementary valuation obstruction; no completeness or choice of a lift of the whole multisection is used.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr; elementary principal-maximal-ideal calculation in the chart of models.tex Tag 0CDC

proof.text: Therefore every point of $B$ maps into $W^{\mathrm{sm}}$. The factorization through its open subscheme is obtained by restricting $b$: on $b^{-1}(V)$ for each open $V\subseteq W^{\mathrm{sm}}$, use the same map of structure sheaves as $b$. These maps agree on overlaps and cover $B$, and their composite with the inclusion is $b$; equivalently this is the open-subscheme description of [def-weil-open-immersion]. This also covers $B=\varnothing$. Taking $B=S$ with its identity finite etale structure gives the section assertion.
